input_text: A computing system stores weights and intermediate values in different memories. During the first pass it reads a prompt and builds a cache of keys and values. During later steps it reads the same stored prefix and appends one new token at a time. A small computation tile can reduce temporary memory while increasing repeated weight reads. These are separate costs. We compare schedules using exactly the same input tokens, numerical precision, compute engines, memory capacity and communication budget. Persistent state remains available between calls, while a temporary activation can be released after its last consumer. The experiment records tensor shapes, numerical errors and cache growth. It does not measure the speed or energy of a future chip. A physical design must also meet port, routing and timing constraints before an end to end benefit can be claimed. Changing a static connection for every decoding step would require a different hardware capability and must be counted explicitly.
scope: Real CPU inference correctness and observed logical tensors; no chip performance, model quality benchmark, or physical partition optimum.
